code.description: Blank fenced and inline code in `source`. `expect.commonmark` is `strip_code`'s output, `expect.skill_export` the output under the skill-export rules. Both keep the number of characters, so offsets here count characters. Under CommonMark a fence is found inside a list item or a block quote (a fence indented to the item's content column opens, and it ends with its container), a backtick after an odd run of `\` is literal, and a code span in a table row (a line starting with `|`) stays in its cell: a `|` not escaped as `\|` ends the cell. Skill-export knows no containers, does not honour the escape and does not cut a row.

inner.description: Parse a wikilink body `inner` (`embed` true reads it as an embed). `expect` is null when there is no link; else `target`, `heading`, `alias`, `target_at` (characters before the target in `inner`) and, when set, `block` and `size`.

url.description: A markdown link URL. `expect.vault_link` is `is_vault_link_url`, `expect.target` is `md_link_target`.

body.description: Scan `body` for links (`options`: `code_rules` as `commonmark`, `skill-export` or `none`, `skip_html_comments`, `self_links`; each optional). `expect.links` are the links in order, each with `kind`, `raw`, `target`, `alias`, `at` (characters before the span), `text` (the source the span covers) and, when set, `heading`, `block`, `size`. `expect.abandoned` lists each `[[` given up on, with `reason`, `at`, `text` and `embed` when a `!` came before it. Every runner also checks that the plain link list agrees with the spanned one. A `!` after an odd run of `\` is escaped: the link is a wikilink that starts at the `[[`.

expect.display: See the thing and img.png and Plain.
